# Exponential base capacity versus actual convex-cap retention

This note distinguishes two exact finite-dimensional quantities. Their
ratio is unbounded with fixed integer dimension n=1 as the continuous
dimension varies, even for affine-root homothetic simplex fibers. Thus an
entropy capacity cannot be converted into an actual integer-centroid
retained mass with a factor depending only on n. This does not refute any
criterion that first selects a special marginal center or optimizing base.

## 1. Two capacities and their exact meanings

Let P be a finite set of positive fibers, with masses w_z>0, and fix
j in conv(P). Define

    E_j=inf_a sum_z w_z exp(a.(z-j)),                  (1)
    T_j=max {sum_z t_z:0<=t_z<=w_z,
                           sum_z (z-j)t_z=0}.         (2)

The exact entropy dual is

    log E_j=max_(lambda>=0, sum lambda=1,
                 sum lambda z=j)
                 sum_z lambda_z log(w_z/lambda_z),    (3)

with the convention `0 log(w/0)=0`.

For completeness, weighted AM--GM gives the lower bound in (3) for every
balanced lambda and every a. If j is in relint conv(P), restrict a to the
linear span of P-j. Its exponential sum is coercive: some fixed relative
ball of radius epsilon about zero lies in conv(P-j), so in every unit
direction one term has exponent at least epsilon|a| and coefficient at
least min w_z. The sum therefore has a minimizer a_*. Its gradient is zero.
The positive probabilities

    lambda_z=w_z exp(a_*.(z-j))/E_j

are balanced and give equality in (3). Strict convexity on that span also
gives uniqueness of a_*. If j lies on a proper minimal face, expose it by
a functional zero on that face and negative elsewhere. Every balanced
lambda is supported on the face. Sending the exponential tilt to infinity
in that exposing direction removes precisely the other terms. Applying
the relative-interior argument on the face proves (3) in this case too.
The exponential infimum need not be attained by a finite a at a boundary
base; no such attainment is claimed there.

Finite box-constrained linear-programming duality gives

    T_j=inf_b sum_z w_z(1+b.(z-j))_+.                 (4)

The scalar inequality `(1+s)_+<=exp(s)` implies

    T_j<=E_j.                                        (5)

Crucially, T_j is not merely a relaxed source capacity. The theorem in
`candidate 46f947c28385c3ea` proves that, for
positive intrinsic dimension, EVERY feasible mass/base-moment vector is
realized by one actual ambient cap of the original convex body. Hence when
j is integer and T_j>0, (2) is exactly the maximum mass of a convex cap-cut
subbody whose TRUE unweighted intrinsic centroid has base j. It is also
an upper bound on the mass of every convex subbody with that centroid.
The resulting centroid belongs to the actual retained mixed set.

No continuous Grünbaum depth is attributed to that mixed centroid. The
primitive-ray representation preserves different mass and moment weights,
and neither this variational identity nor an exponential tilt removes that
difference.

## 2. A five-fiber exact obstruction already in continuous dimension four

Let T be the standard 4-simplex, of volume v, and let

    C={ (z,x):1<=z<=5, x in zT }.

This is a full-dimensional convex frustum; its five integer fibers are
exactly `zT`, z=1,...,5. Work in the common volume unit v, so their weights
are `w_z=z^4`. Choose the integer anchor j=3.

The dual b=-1 in (4) gives

    T_3<=3*1+2*16+1*81=116.

Keeping all masses at z=1,2,3 and mass18 at z=4 attains this bound: its
mass is 1+16+81+18=116 and its base moment relative to 3 is
`-2*1-1*16+1*18=0`. It is realized explicitly by the convex cap

    sum_i x_i+3(z-4)<=18^(1/4).

Indeed `2<18^(1/4)<3`, so all fibers z<=3 are retained, z=5 is excluded,
and the retained part at z=4 is `18^(1/4)T`, of volume18v. Thus the actual
maximum cap-subbody mass is exactly116v.

The balanced probabilities

    lambda=(1,4,6,4,1)/16

have mean3. Equation (3), or weighted AM--GM directly, yields

    E_3^16 >= product_(z=1)^5 (16 z^4 / binom(4,z-1))^binom(4,z-1)
             =2^90 3^18 5^4.

Since

    2^42 3^18 5^4 > 29^16,

one has `E_3^16>232^16` and hence

    E_3>232=2T_3.                                    (6)

The integer comparison is reproduced exactly in the accompanying verifier.
Multiplying by v restores ordinary volumes throughout. Thus the proposed
factor `2^n` already fails at n=1,d=4 in an actual convex-compatible family.

## 3. A three-fiber exact variant

A particularly short alternative has d=40 and affine-root fibers at
indices -1,0,1 with scale factors `9/10,1,11/10`, respectively. Again
normalize all masses by the common simplex volume. At j=0, balancing two
endpoint masses requires that they agree, so

    T_0=1+2(9/10)^40,
    E_0=1+2(99/100)^20.

The second formula follows by minimizing the two exponential endpoint
terms, whose minimum is twice their geometric mean. Bernoulli's inequality
gives `(99/100)^20>=4/5`, while the exact integer comparison
`8*9^20<10^20` gives `(9/10)^40<1/8`. Consequently

    E_0>=13/5 > 5/2 > 2T_0.

The retained moment capacity is attained by a cap of the actual body by
Section 1. The anchor is a retained/tilted centroid base; it is not asserted
to equal the original unweighted base centroid.

## 4. No bound depending only on integer dimension

Fix N>=1, put `K=2N+1` and `S_2=sum_(k=1)^N k^2`. Let L be an integer
with `L>=2S_2`, set

    d=L^3,  delta=L^(-2),
    C={ (z,x):-N<=z<=N, x in (1+delta z)T_d },

and choose j=0. All scale factors are strictly positive, since L>N, and
this is again an actual full-dimensional affine-root simplex frustum.
Its integer weights in units of `|T_d|` are

    w_z=(1+z/L^2)^(L^3),    z=-N,...,N.

Uniform probabilities on these bases are balanced. Their AM--GM bound is

    E_0>=K [product_(k=1)^N (1-k^2/L^4)^(L^3)]^(1/K)
        >=K(1-S_2/L)^(1/K).                           (7)

The last inequality is elementary: the product of numbers `1-t_k` with
`t_k>=0` is at least `1-sum t_k`, and Bernoulli's inequality then raises
this lower bound to the integer power L^3. Its argument is positive
because `S_2/L<=1/2`.

For the upper bound choose a=-L in (1). Since `log(1+t)<=t` for t>-1,
each tilted weight is at most one. Therefore

    E_0<=K.                                           (8)

On the other hand the hinge choice b=-1 gives

    1<=T_0<=1+sum_(k=1)^N (k+1)(1-k/L^2)^(L^3)
              <=1+[N(N+3)/2] 2^(-L).                 (9)

For the second inequality, Bernoulli applied to the reciprocal yields
`(1-k/L^2)^(-L^2)>=1+k`. Hence
`(1-k/L^2)^(L^3)<=(1+k)^(-L)<=2^(-L)`. The lower bound retains just the
unit-mass central fiber.

For every fixed N, (7)--(9) prove, as L tends to infinity through integers,

    E_0 -> 2N+1,       T_0 ->1,
    E_0/T_0 ->2N+1.                                  (10)

Given any proposed constant depending only on n=1, choose N so that
2N+1 exceeds it and then choose finite L large enough. Thus no such
universal fixed-anchor entropy-to-cap-retention factor exists. These are
exact inequalities on actual fibers; no continuous approximation of the
integer sums or numerical minimization is used.

The example does NOT assert that anchor0 is a weighted marginal center,
the optimal base for another variational objective, or the true centroid
base of the original source. It therefore closes the fixed-anchor capacity
conversion, not every possible integer-base selection rule and not OC.
